note:
INSTRUMENT NOT BUILT. What it must do: for every skill in the derived canon set, establish that something reaches it -- the `/in-session` language table, a `chains_to:` from another skill, or a documented invocation by name -- and that what it chains TO exists. LIVENESS IS TRANSITIVE AND THAT IS THE DIRECTION NOBODY CHECKS: a skill with a live caller is still dead if the thing it chains to was retired, and the caller looks healthy throughout. vc split this off `AC-00.5` for exactly that reason -- buried under the retirement half, the transitive direction had no instrument and would have been swept. THE POSITIVE CONTROL: plant a `chains_to:` naming a skill that does not exist and the check must fire; plant an orphan skill nothing references and it must fire too. A checker that only walks FROM the roster finds the second and never the first.
BUILT AND GREEN 2026-09-02: `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/every_skill_has_a_live_caller.rs`. Four arms. The shipped tree: 23 skills, 13 declaring `chains_to`, ZERO dangling chains and ZERO unreached skills. Two controls as the note demanded -- a chain naming a skill that does not exist MUST fire (the transitive direction, and the reason vc split this row off AC-00.5), and a skill nothing reaches MUST fire.

AND A THIRD ARM THE NOTE DID NOT ASK FOR, WHICH THE MEASUREMENT FORCED. SEVEN shipped skills are chained to by NOTHING -- in-session, in-review, in-plan, in-debug, in-autopsy, in-cost-analysis, in-tca-init -- and every one is an ENTRY POINT an operator types, each referenced as `/name` in usage-rules.md. A checker that knew only `chains_to` would report seven dead skills, ALL FALSE, and a checker with seven standing false positives is one nobody runs twice. So liveness has two legitimate routes -- a `chains_to` from another skill, or a `/name` invocation in a canon document -- and the third arm holds that an entry point is live, with its own inverse arm so it cannot pass for a predicate that never reports anything.

REACH DECLARED: this establishes that something REFERS to each skill, not that the reference is honoured at run time. A document naming `/in-review` in a sentence nobody follows still counts as a caller here; whether the instruction is followable is AC-00.2's read.
